text:
[name]
Chicago, IL · [email] · [phone] · [url]

CHIEF OPERATING OFFICER

Eighteen years across strategy consulting and consumer operating roles. Partner at Bain & Company (consumer products practice), then Chief Operating Officer of a publicly traded consumer company with 5,000 employees and about $2.0 billion in revenue, where I led a three-year turnaround: operating margin from 4.1% to 11.8%, net debt reduced by $600 million, and a share price that rose from $14 to $41 over the period. Independent director on two public boards.

EXECUTIVE EXPERIENCE

Harvest Lane Brands, Inc. (NYSE-listed; packaged foods; about $2.0B revenue; 5,000 employees; 9 plants) — Chicago, IL
Chief Operating Officer (Sep 2020 – Present)
Report to the CEO. Responsible for supply chain, manufacturing, procurement, quality, customer service, and the company's three business units (retail brands, food service, private label). About 4,600 of the company's 5,000 employees sit in my organization. Member of the executive committee and the disclosure committee.
• Led the 2021–2024 operational turnaround ("Project Reset"): adjusted operating margin from 4.1% (FY2020) to 11.8% (FY2024); adjusted EBITDA from $150M to $335M; free cash flow from negative $40M to positive $210M.
• Consolidated the manufacturing network from 13 plants to 9 while increasing output 6%; $95M of annual fixed-cost savings, delivered on the schedule and budget announced to investors in 2021.
• Rebuilt procurement: moved 70% of spend to indexed contracts and a central category team; $120M of annual savings against a $2.4B cost base, verified by the audit committee's third-party review.
• Paid down $600M of net debt from operating cash flow and the sale of a non-core snacks business ($180M, closed 2023); leverage from 4.9x to 2.1x adjusted EBITDA.
• Share price $14 (Sep 2020) to $41 (Sep 2024); total shareholder return of about 215% versus 48% for the packaged-food peer index over the same period.
• Reduced customer order fill rate issues: on-time-in-full from 88% to 97%; retailer compliance fines fell from $22M to $4M a year.
• Safety: total recordable incident rate from 3.4 to 1.1 across 9 plants; no fatalities during the tenure.
• Led the integration of a $320M acquisition (2024): synergy target of $35M achieved in 14 months against a 24-month plan.
• Built the executive team for operations: hired 5 of 7 direct reports; two have since been promoted into general manager roles.
• Stood up the company's first integrated business planning process (monthly S&OP across the three units); forecast accuracy at the SKU-week level improved from 61% to 79%, and finished-goods inventory fell by $140M while service levels rose.
• Sponsored the digital manufacturing program: sensor-based predictive maintenance in all 9 plants, unplanned downtime down 27%; the program was presented to investors at the 2024 capital markets day.
• Serve as the executive sponsor for the company's employee resource groups and chair the operations talent review; 38% of plant-manager promotions in 2023–2025 went to internal candidates from the operations leadership program I started.

Bain & Company — Chicago and London
Partner, Consumer Products Practice (Jan 2016 – Aug 2020)
Principal (Jan 2013 – Dec 2015) · Manager (2010 – 2012) · Consultant and Associate Consultant (2006 – 2009)
• Led the North American consumer products operations practice for three years; practice revenue grew from $60M to $115M under my leadership; team of 11 partners and about 120 consultants.
• Served as lead partner for six Fortune 500 consumer companies on cost transformation, supply chain redesign, and post-merger integration; programs with announced savings of about $1.4B in aggregate.
• Led the integration planning for a $7B food-industry merger (2018–2019), including the synergy case presented to both boards.
• Authored two practice publications on supply chain resilience cited in the business press; frequent speaker at the Consumer Goods Forum.
• Promoted to Partner in 10 years from Associate Consultant, two years ahead of the standard track.
• Spent 2011–2012 in the London office leading European grocery projects.

EDUCATION

Stanford Graduate School of Business — M.B.A., 2010. Arjay Miller Scholar (top 10% of the class). Siebel Scholar.
Princeton University — A.B., Economics, magna cum laude, 2006. Phi Beta Kappa. Senior thesis prize in the department.

BOARD AND ADVISORY ROLES

Independent Director, Clearwater Outdoor Holdings (Nasdaq-listed outdoor equipment; $1.1B revenue), 2023 – Present. Chair of the operations and sustainability committee; member of the audit committee.
Independent Director, Meridian Foods Corporation (NYSE-listed food distributor; $3.4B revenue), 2024 – Present. Member of the compensation committee.
Trustee, Greater Chicago Food Depository, 2019 – Present; chair of the operations committee during the 2020–2021 demand surge (distribution volume up 60%).
Advisory council member, Stanford Graduate School of Business Center for Social Innovation, 2021 – Present.

RECOGNITION AND SPEAKING

Named one of the Chicago Tribune's Top 25 business executives, 2024. Fortune "turnaround to watch" feature, 2023. Keynote speaker at the Consumer Goods Forum Supply Chain Summit (2022, 2024) and at the National Association of Manufacturers annual meeting (2025). Guest lecturer, Kellogg School of Management operations course (annually since 2021).

ADDITIONAL
Series 24-style governance training completed through the NACD Directorship Certification (2023). Languages: English (native), French (professional working proficiency). Interests: competitive rowing (masters national championships, 2022 and 2024), restoring mid-century furniture.
